name: Weeb Central
_todo: Real WeebCentral.kt uses one endpoint for popular/latest/search: GET /search/data?text=&limit=32&offset={page*32}&display_mode=Full+Display&sort=<value>, where <value> differs per mode ('Popularity' for popular, 'Latest Updates' for latest, empty for plain search) plus several UriFilter-driven query params (status/tag/type/official-translation/adult-content/author). This schema's {page} placeholder assumes page-number pagination, not offset math, so 'popular'/'latest' below hardcode sort= and use {page} directly in an offset-style query param as an approximation -- verify the real offset math (offset=(page-1)*32) once a live test is possible.

Chapter list is NOT at {manga_url} -- the real flow extracts a numeric seriesId from the manga URL's second path segment, then fetches GET /series/{seriesId}/full-chapter-list separately. This schema has no 'extract a path segment and build a new URL from it' primitive, so chapter_list's path below assumes {manga_url} already ends in a form appendable with /full-chapter-list, which is NOT what the real site expects -- this endpoint is very likely wrong until the runtime supports path-segment extraction.

Page list needs baseUrl + chapter path + '/images?is_prev=False&reading_style=long_strip' appended, not the raw chapter URL -- approximated below by folding those query params into the endpoint template's static path, assuming {chapter_url} is a path (not a full URL with its own query string already).

Real extension sets custom image request headers (Accept: image/avif,image/webp,*/*, Host: <image host>) and removes the default Origin header entirely -- this schema's client.extra_headers only supports static addition, not removal, and page-image fetches reuse the general 'client' headers rather than per-image overrides. Images may fail to load if weebcentral's CDN enforces those headers strictly.

Rate limited to 1 request per 2 seconds by the real extension (HTTP 429 was a real reported bug at higher rates) -- this schema has no rate_limit field, so a naive scraper here risks 429s that the real Kotlin extension avoids.
